message.content: Lions mate during the breeding season (typically spring and summer). A male will approach a receptive female, often after establishing dominance through scent marking and vocalizations. If the female is receptive, she will lower her head and allow the male to mount. The male mounts from behind, and copulation lasts only a few minutes. After mating, the male may guard the female or leave; females usually mate with multiple males over a short period, leading to mixed paternity within a litter.
